summary: The uncommitted M7 diff (20 modified files plus the new api/, auth/apiKey, routes/api/v1, routes/docs/api, migration and e2e files; HEAD 07ff966, nothing staged) implements the brief and plan.md. Each of the 29 operations is defined once in api/endpoints.ts with its Zod schemas. The 21 route files are thin endpoint() wrappers that only call guards, services and serializers, plus a fallback for 405. The OpenAPI 3.1 document is built from the same definitions with z.toJSONSchema (no new dependency, choice recorded in PLAN.md). openapi.db.spec.ts proves the routes and endpoints match one-to-one and that every $ref resolves. requireApiKey gives 401 for missing, malformed, unknown, tampered and revoked keys before params are parsed. requireApiTournament gives the same 404 for other-org and missing tournaments. lastUsedAt is throttled to 60 s. One envelope covers Zod 400 with issues, ServiceError.kind 409/422/404, the [...path] 404 and 405. Results set with a key go through setMatchResult as api_key reports, and reports for a player go through the shared report() state machine. Key messages are organizer messages labelled with the copied key name, published over SSE and shown with badges. The migration is drizzle-generated and minimal (author_id nullable, api_key_name). /docs/api uses Paraglide strings, landmarks, headings, table headers and theme tokens, and is linked from the footer and the API keys tab. PLAN.md has M7 ✅ and its notes, and the README has a REST API section. I re-ran check (0 errors/0 warnings), lint, test:unit (29 files/332 tests) and the full e2e suite (11 passed). Only minor issues remain. SvelteKit's CSRF check answers mutating requests without a content type with a plain-text 403 that bypasses the envelope; this is documented, and the fix needs a CSRF config decision from the user. Three match routes act on bye ids that GET answers with 404. Option-less modules accept arbitrary requirement config. The spec lists a 'bye' status the API never returns. About half the route handlers are never executed by tests. Full review: .agents/tasks/m7-rest-api/2026-10-30-180413-review.md (also review.md).

findings.detail: In production builds, SvelteKit's CSRF check (node_modules/@sveltejs/kit/src/runtime/server/csrf.js) runs before handle. It answers POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE that have no content type (or a form type) and no matching Origin with a plain-text 403 'Cross-site POST form submissions are forbidden', not the error envelope. Body-less calls such as POST …/start or DELETE …/result from curl, fetch or requests hit it unless they send Content-Type: application/json. I reproduced this against the built server. It is documented in the docs page, OpenAPI info.description, README and PLAN.md. If the user wants the envelope everywhere: set kit.csrf.checkOrigin: false and re-apply the same origin check in hooks.server.ts for paths outside /api/v1/. The API is authenticated only by the Authorization header, so CSRF can't apply to it. This changes a framework security default, so it needs the user's go-ahead first.

Bye matches are stored as rows but getMatch returns undefined for them, so GET …/matches/{id} and GET …/messages answer a bye id with 404. POST …/messages only checks that the row belongs to the tournament, so it stores and publishes a message on a bye and returns 201. DELETE …/result (result/+server.ts) and DELETE …/help (help/+server.ts) call clearMatchResult/clearHelp before matchDetail returns 404, so they write and then answer 'not found'. Call getMatch (404 if undefined) before the service in these three handlers, as GET …/messages already does.

parseModuleConfig returns the raw config unchanged when a module has no tournamentConfig. The admin form always produces {} for such modules, but PUT …/requirements stores whatever object the client sends (e.g. discord with arbitrary keys) as jsonb, and GET returns it. Return { ok: true, config: {} } in that case, or reject a non-empty config, so the API can't create state the admin page can't.

MATCH_STATUSES includes 'bye', so Match.status and the listMatches ?status= filter document a value the API never returns: listMatches drops byes, so ?status=bye is always []. Drop 'bye' from the API enum (keep the satisfies check against MatchProgress) so the spec matches the 'byes are left out' description.

About half the route handlers only pass the route coverage test and are never executed: PATCH /tournaments/{id} (merge with the current values plus the startsAt transform), PUT theme, GET/PUT requirements, unpublish, open-check-in, start-next-stage, shuffle, PUT check-in, DELETE participant, DELETE tournament, DELETE result, DELETE help and GET messages. Add a db spec that imports a few route modules and calls their exported handlers with a fake event, at least PATCH (partial update keeps the other fields; startsAt ISO → Date) and PUT requirements (422 for an unknown module, 409 after start). handler.db.spec.ts already has the pattern.
